study type: Nested case-control study within a multicenter cohort study
exposure: Diastolic blood pressure at 20 weeks gestation
Body mass index at first prenatal visit
cohort: 1165 nulliparous healthy pregnant women in Brazil
finding: Higher body mass index at the first prenatal visit and diastolic blood pressure ≥ 75 mmHg at 20 weeks gestation were independently associated with preeclampsia, which in turn was associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Women with preeclampsia had a higher incidence of cesarean sections compared to controls.
birth_weight: Measured, mean difference of 379g lower in the preeclampsia group
